newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK SHARES END UP FOR THIRD STRAIGHT 97 SESSION.
newsitem.headline: GREEK SHARES END UP FOR THIRD STRAIGHT 97 SESSION.

text.p: Greek shares surged ahead to close 2.55 percent higher, with strong gains for the third consecutive trading session of 1997.

The general share index was led higher by banks, industrials and construction stocks. Market analysts said the bourse was being propelled by a general belief in political stability in 1997 and positive economic fundamentals.

"The bourse discounts political stability and good macroeconomic fundamentals, mainly lower inflation and interest rates, and positive corporate earnings in 1997," said Costas Panagidis, general director at Axon Securities SA.

Bankers and economists polled by Reuters on Tuesday said they expected CPI inflation to fall to 7.5 percent year-on-year in December from 7.7 percent in November. Forecasts ranged from 7.4 percent to 7.6 percent.
Press reports have said CPI-based inflation will be at 7.4 percent year-on-year in December. The inflation figure will be released on Wednesday.

"The general index is heading towards the 1050 level after it broke out of the 980 resistance today," said Panagidis. "Banks have been the locomotive of the bourse so far but the bellweather sector to watch is construction."
He added that the bourse has done traditionally well in the first half of January and this provides a positive backdrop for an advance to higher levels in the next few days.

The Athens general index rose 2.55 percent or 24.59 points to 989.98 points from Friday's 965.39 points. Turnover was 8.69 billion drachmas on volume of 2.79 million shares, boosted by active block trading.
Bank, construction and industrial shares led the advance with the sectoral indexes jumping 3.61 percent, 2.90 percent and 2.46 percent respectively.
"It is interesting that small cap listings show signs of invigoration after a long time," said Panagidis. The small-cap index rose 1.29 percent to 73.85 points.
Gainers led decliners 134 to 69 with 24 shares unchanged on 227 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 569.00-587.00. Shares of OTE telecom the underlying, climbed 55 drachmas to close at 4,450.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $12.25-$13.25. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted at 4,765-5,057 drachmas. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
